events.title: Magnitude 7.4 Earthquake Strikes Chocó
events.detail: At 07:34 local time (12:34 UTC), a magnitude 7.4–7.5 earthquake ruptured roughly 20 km east of San José del Palmar, Chocó Department, at a depth of 96–110 km within the subducting Nazca Plate (an unusual intermediate-depth supra-slab rupture). Shaking lasted up to two minutes and was felt across western and central Colombia and in parts of Ecuador and Panama. USGS put the depth at 110.3 km; Colombia's Servicio Geológico Colombiano (SGC) put it at 96 km, and initially reported the magnitude as only 6.7 before revising it upward to 7.4.

events.title: First Major Aftershock (M4.8–5.0) Strikes at 08:18
events.detail: Roughly 44 minutes after the main shock, a magnitude 4.8 (SGC) / 5.0 (USGS) aftershock struck near the same epicentral zone, followed by a magnitude 3.8 event at 10:01. Over 100 aftershocks were recorded on the first day alone.

events.title: Early Death Toll Reaches 132
events.detail: Within hours of the quake, Colombian authorities reported the death toll had risen to 132 as rescue teams began combing collapsed buildings in Cali, Pereira, and Quibdó.

events.title: President Declares National Disaster and Three-Day Mourning
events.detail: Just three days into his term, President Abelardo de la Espriella declared a state of national disaster and three days of national mourning, traveling immediately to the Unified Command Post at the UNGRD to direct the federal response.

sources.name: Semana — De la Espriella primeras horas

events.title: Seven Airports Suspend Operations
events.detail: Colombia's civil aviation authority suspended flights at seven airports — Pereira (Matecaña), Manizales, Quibdó, Armenia (El Edén), Cartago, Buenaventura, and Cali (Alfonso Bonilla Aragón) — after runway and terminal damage was reported.

events.title: University Hospital of Valle Partially Collapses in Cali
events.detail: The Hospital Universitario del Valle in Cali sustained damage to roughly 70% of its infrastructure, forcing the evacuation of more than 600 patients even as the facility remained a hub for treating quake casualties.

events.title: Matecaña Airport Partial Collapse Kills 3 in Pereira
events.detail: A section of Pereira's Matecaña International Airport terminal partially collapsed during the quake, killing three people on site.

era: Search, Rescue and Political Crisis (11–15 August)

events.title: Death Toll Reaches 188 Across Capital Cities
events.detail: Confirmed fatalities across departmental capitals — Quibdó, Pereira, Manizales, Cali, Armenia and Popayán — reached 188, with 1,677 people reported injured, according to Asocapitales' tracking of municipal reports.

events.title: Bogotá Deploys 100 Rescue Workers to Cali
events.detail: The capital dispatched an initial 100 rescue specialists to Cali; by August 11 this grew to over 220 rescue specialists and 100 military engineers working the city's collapsed structures.

events.title: UNGRD Director Pava Declines International Rescue Teams
events.detail: Javier Pava, the outgoing UNGRD director held over from the Petro administration, sent a letter to the Foreign Ministry on August 11 asserting Colombia had sufficient domestic search-and-rescue capacity and that the priority should be logistical and material aid rather than foreign rescue teams — a call that would become highly controversial as the survival window narrowed.

events.title: Colombian Red Cross Deploys Teams to Antioquia, Quindío, Caldas, Chocó
events.detail: The Colombian Red Cross expanded relief operations, sending teams to Antioquia, Quindío and Caldas departments, and 30 personnel directly into Chocó to support the epicentral response.

events.title: President Declares Economic Emergency
events.detail: De la Espriella declared a state of economic emergency, granting the executive three months of decree powers to reallocate budget, offer tax relief and mobilize extraordinary reconstruction spending without needing Congressional approval.

events.title: Mexican 'Topos' Rescue Teams Join the Search
events.detail: Independent Mexican rescue brigades — Topos de Tlatelolco and Topos Aztecas, some redeployed from earthquake relief in Caracas, Venezuela — joined search efforts in Cali on August 12, arriving even as the Colombian government's formal restrictions on foreign rescue personnel remained in place.

events.title: Colombia Limits Accepted Rescue Teams to Four Countries
events.detail: As the 72-hour survival window closed, Colombia said it would formally accept international rescue teams from only four countries — the United States, Ecuador, El Salvador and Israel — a decision that drew criticism from nations whose offers were declined.

events.title: Death Toll Hits 265 — Deadliest Colombian Quake Since the 1990s
events.detail: The confirmed death toll passed 265 with 3,494 injured, making it Colombia's deadliest earthquake since the 1990s.

events.title: Pava Letter Scandal Breaks Publicly, Toll at 285
events.detail: Pava's letter declining specialized foreign rescue teams became public, triggering national outrage as the death toll reached 285 with 3,975 injured and 379 missing. Critics accused the outgoing UNGRD leadership of costing lives during the critical rescue window.

events.title: 80-Person Israeli Delegation Lands in Cali
events.detail: An 80-person Israeli aid delegation — including personnel from the IDF, Defense Ministry and Foreign Affairs Ministry — landed in Cali to assist rescue operations, one of the four foreign teams formally accepted.

events.title: Pava Removed from UNGRD; Tamayo Takes Over
events.detail: Javier Pava was removed as UNGRD director on August 14 and replaced by David Santiago Tamayo. Colombia subsequently widened acceptance of international rescue assistance. Pava defended himself publicly, saying "Yo sí acepté la ayuda" ("I did accept the aid"), arguing his original position reflected only first-hours needs and had already changed the same day it was issued.

events.title: Death Toll Reaches 281, 379 Reported Missing
events.detail: Confirmed deaths rose to 281 with more than 12,000 homes destroyed and 379 people reported missing as rescue operations continued.

events.title: Goldman Sachs Cuts Colombia's 2026 Growth Forecast
events.detail: Goldman Sachs reduced its 2026 GDP growth forecast for Colombia citing the earthquake's economic disruption, even as Oxford Economics maintained its unchanged 3% forecast, illustrating a divergence in analyst assessments of the disaster's macro impact.

events.title: Search and Rescue Operations Extend to August 15
events.detail: Formal search and rescue operations, initially bound by the standard 72-hour survival window, were extended through August 15. At least 38 people were pulled alive from the rubble over the course of the operation.

events.title: President Visits Quibdó, Pledges 'Marshall Plan' for Chocó
events.detail: De la Espriella traveled to Quibdó on August 16, distributing soccer balls to children in one of the most devastated areas and insisting that although Chocó's monetary losses were comparatively smaller, it suffered the worst humanitarian toll and deserved a dedicated reconstruction plan to settle the department's historic infrastructure debts.

events.title: President Delivers First Official Balance: 289 Dead, 4,187 Injured
events.detail: In his first official presidential address on the disaster, de la Espriella confirmed 289 deaths, 4,187 injured and 143 missing, and cited a preliminary private-sector damage estimate of roughly COP 30 trillion (about US$9.6B) — COP 24.5 trillion in buildings and COP 5.5 trillion in public infrastructure networks. He closed with: "La tierra tembló, pero Colombia no se quebró" ("The earth shook, but Colombia did not break").

events.title: Shakira Pledges $1M and 10 New Schools for Chocó
events.detail: Colombian singer Shakira announced a $1 million donation for school reconstruction, committing to build 10 new schools and contribute to rebuilding the University of Chocó.

events.title: 'Fondo Milagro' Reconstruction Fund Created
events.detail: The government created the "Fondo Milagro" (Miracle Fund) to centralize and transparently manage domestic and international donations, channeling contributions toward rebuilding hospitals, schools, buildings, roads and airports damaged by the quake.

events.title: President Warns Against Corruption in Aid Collection
events.detail: De la Espriella issued a public warning against corruption in the handling of earthquake relief donations, promising "austerity and transparency" and stating that anyone found diverting funds "se las verá conmigo" ("will have to answer to me").

events.title: Colombian Peso Stabilizes Despite Quake-Driven Volatility
events.detail: After a volatile week following the earthquake and government transition, the Colombian peso closed at COP 3,133.25 per USD on August 18, down from an opening of COP 3,149 earlier in the week.

events.title: Death Toll Reaches 312, Ten Days After the Quake
events.detail: Colombia's National Institute of Legal Medicine reported 312+ confirmed deaths, 4,611+ injured, and 290+ still missing as of August 19, nearly ten days after the earthquake struck.
events.confidenceReason: Figures continue to evolve as search operations and identification of remains proceed.

events.title: 325+ Aftershocks Recorded Since the Main Shock
events.detail: The Servicio Geológico Colombiano recorded more than 325 aftershocks in the epicentral region since August 10, keeping structural-risk assessments active in Chocó, Valle del Cauca and Risaralda.

events.title: Starlink Provides Free Internet to Five Departments
events.detail: Starlink announced free internet service across five affected departments through September 12, supporting communications for relief coordination and displaced families.

events.title: World Bank Announces $200M Emergency Financing, Weighs $450M Loan
events.detail: The World Bank announced US$200 million in emergency financing, while Colombia's Finance Minister Miguel Gómez Martínez said the government would seek up to US$450 million in additional World Bank financing, against a total reconstruction estimate that at one point ran as high as US$6.4 billion.

events.title: President Signs Decree 1261, Declaring Economic Emergency in 15 Departments
events.detail: President Abelardo de la Espriella signed Decree 1261 of 2026, declaring a state of economic, social and ecological emergency for 30 days across the 15 departments affected by the earthquake — Antioquia, Caldas, Cauca, Chocó, Quindío, Cundinamarca, Risaralda, Huila, Valle del Cauca, Tolima, Putumayo, Norte de Santander, Bolívar, Nariño and Sucre. The decree grants the Executive extraordinary powers to issue temporary legislative measures: financing reconstruction, modifying the national budget, tapping the General Royalties System, and granting temporary tax, customs and currency relief.

events.title: Death Toll Rises to 319 as Emergency Decree Takes Effect
events.detail: UNGRD's 20 August 06:30 report put the toll at 319 dead, 4,506 injured, 260 missing and 364 rescued alive, with more than 30,000 homes destroyed and roughly 170,000 damaged across 476 municipios — the assessment underpinning the same-day economic emergency decree.
events.confidenceReason: Figures continue to evolve as search operations and identification of remains proceed.

events.title: President Delivers New Balance: 329 Dead, 4,600 Injured, 247 Missing
events.detail: In a balance cut off at 18:30 on Aug 21 (published Aug 22), President de la Espriella reported 329 deaths, 4,600 injured and 247 missing, with 154,014 families (314,751 people) affected across 16 departments and 481 municipios. Structural damage included 31,183 homes destroyed, 171,273 damaged, 553 buildings collapsed and 5,755 damaged, plus 3,710 schools, 5,584 community centers and 367 health centers affected.

media.caption: President de la Espriella presents the updated earthquake balance

events.confidenceReason: Figures continue to evolve as search operations and identification of remains proceed.

events.title: Cali's Search-and-Rescue Phase Formally Concludes, City Toll at 150
events.detail: Cali's formal search-and-rescue operation concluded on Aug 22 with the city's confirmed death toll revised to 150 as authorities reconciled duplicate and unconfirmed records — down slightly from the earlier 153 figure reported in the department-level breakdown.

media.caption: Search and rescue teams continue operations among the rubble

events.title: Major Banks Cut Mortgage Rates to 8% for Quake Victims
events.detail: Grupo Aval, Banco GNB Sudameris and Grupo Bolívar agreed to reduce mortgage interest rates to 8% effective annual for earthquake victims for the life of the loan, a decision President de la Espriella publicly thanked: "Aceptaron. Mi gratitud por esta decisión." Separately, Bancolombia lowered its own housing loan rate from 14% to 8% effective annual, though only for loans disbursed from Aug 25 onward, with eligibility criteria still unpublished.

media.caption: Reconstruction financing remains limited to a handful of bank and city commitments

events.title: Private Sector Donations Surpass COP 2 Trillion
events.detail: Private-sector donations for earthquake reconstruction surpassed COP 2 trillion (~US$651M) by Aug 21, led by contributors including Jaime Gilinski and Raquel Kardonski de Gilinski (focused on Cali hospitals, health centers and schools), Luis Carlos Sarmiento Angulo, David Vélez, Juan Carlos Mora, Davivienda, Seguros Bolívar, Tecnoquímicas, ProAntioquia and ProPacífico. Separately, Asobancaria member banks extended COP 1.1 trillion in credit relief — grace periods of up to 12 months, interest forgiveness, suspension of legal collection proceedings and credit-history protection.

media.caption: Colombian business leaders channel donations toward reconstruction

events.title: New Shallow Aftershocks Recorded Near Istmina, Chocó
events.detail: The Servicio Geológico Colombiano recorded a magnitude 3.1 tremor in Istmina, Chocó on the evening of Aug 22, followed by two more shallow events on the morning of Aug 23 — magnitude 2.6 at 06:50 local and magnitude 2.8 at 07:49 local — underscoring continued seismic unrest near the epicentral zone nearly two weeks after the main shock.

media.caption: SGC records new shallow tremors near Istmina, Chocó

events.title: President Announces September 7 Visit to Chocó With Business Leaders
events.detail: President de la Espriella announced he will travel to Chocó on Sept. 7 together with major business leaders to design a dedicated recovery plan for the department, continuing his earlier pledge of a 'Marshall Plan' for Chocó's historic infrastructure gap.

media.caption: Recovery coordination continues in earthquake-affected regions
